I believe the government should pursue providing all citizens a universal basic income (UBI) funded by higher taxes on the wealthy. This policy aligns with values of equity, dignity, and economic security, ensuring that everyone has access to a baseline level of financial stability. In an era of increasing automation and precarious work, UBI can act as a safety net, empowering individuals to pursue education, caregiving, or entrepreneurial ventures without the constant pressure of financial insecurity. It also acknowledges the systemic inequalities perpetuated by wealth concentration, where the richest often benefit disproportionately from economic growth while others struggle to meet basic needs.

Higher taxes on the wealthy are a fair and necessary means to fund UBI. Progressive taxation ensures that those who have benefited most from societal resources contribute more to its collective well-being. This approach fosters a more balanced and inclusive economy, reducing extreme wealth disparities that undermine social cohesion. Critics argue that UBI might disincentivize work, but evidence from pilot programs suggests otherwise—most recipients use the funds to improve their lives while continuing to contribute to society. Ultimately, UBI represents a bold step toward a more just and compassionate society, where everyone has the opportunity to thrive, not just survive.
